final_message:
I couldn't reproduce this, so I haven't changed anything. In this repo `is_leap_year(1900)` already returns `False`.

The only definition is in `src/leap.py`:
```python
return (y % 4 == 0 and y % 100 != 0) or y % 400 == 0
```
This is the correct Gregorian rule. I ran it for several years and got 1900 → False, 2000 → True, 2023 → False, 2024 → True and 2100 → False. The only other file that mentions leap years is `tests/test_leap.py`, which I didn't open.

The users may be running a different version, such as an older release or a copy of the code elsewhere. A caller that does its own `year % 4 == 0` check would also give this result. If you can tell me how they call it or which version they have, I can look further.
